newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish fixed bond yields seen flat in large demand.
newsitem.headline: Polish fixed bond yields seen flat in large demand.

text.p: Yields on Polish 12-percent five-year fixed interest bonds and 15-percent two-year bonds are expected to hold flat at Wednesday's joint 800 million zloty primary tender amid large foreign demand, analysts said.
They said yields on the five-year paper should be around 18.55 percent and around 20.60 percent for the two-year bonds, relatively unchanged from the last auction on February 5.
"Foreign players are likely to show a lot of interest in the tender with little demand expected from domestic banks," said Wojciech Kowalczyk, senior dealer at Bank Handlowy SA.
Dealers said investors' bids were likely to total between 800 million and one billion zlotys on Wednesday.

The value date for the auction is March 12, 1997, with the five year bonds maturing on June 12, 2002, and the two-year paper due on June 12, 1999. The tender will be held at 1100 local time (1000 GMT), an hour earlier than in the past.
